chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the one in Ihram has intercourse with his wife before he comes to Al-Muzdalifa, then upon him is (performing) the Hajj next year.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَةَ: Al-Muzdalifa, a sacred site visited during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim who has intercourse with his wife before reaching Muzdalifa?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the penalty of 'Hajj min qabil' (repeating Hajj the following year) for a pilgrim who consummates marriage before reaching Al-Muzdalifa, distinguishing it from the penalty of staying in the current year. This ruling highlights the severity of breaking the sanctity of Ihram during the critical pre-Muzdalifa phase, a view supported by prominent Shia jurists who emphasize the continuity of the pilgrimage state. It serves as a key legal precedent for determining whether a Hajj is considered complete or requires repetition based on the timing of the breach.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the one in Ihraam falls upon his wife before he comes to Al-Muzdalifa, so upon him is (performing of) the Hajj next year’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one performs sexual intercourse with his wife before coming to al-Muzdalifah, he is required to perform al-Hajj in future.’”
